content: Drug interactions can alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the likelihood of severe side effects. This document does not include all potential drug interactions. It is essential to maintain a comprehensive list of all products you use, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal supplements, and share this information with your healthcare provider and pharmacist. Certain medications can influence the elimination of praziquantel from your body, potentially affecting its efficacy. Examples of such drugs include azole antifungals (e.g., itraconazole, ketoconazole), chloroquine, cimetidine, dexamethasone, efavirenz, macrolide antibiotics (e.g., erythromycin), and rifamycins (e.g., rifampin). In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call 911. Otherwise, contact a poison control center without delay. U.S. residents can reach the poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. While taking this medication, laboratory and/or medical tests, such as urine or stool examinations and biopsies of infected tissue, should be conducted as necessary. If you have a pre-existing heart condition, additional monitoring may be required. Ensure that you attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Avoid flushing medications down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly dispose of this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in May 2024. It is important to note that this document provides a summary and does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Common side effects of this medication may include headache, dizziness, stomach pain, nausea, fatigue, weakness, joint or muscle pain, loss of appetite, vomiting, and sweating. These side effects are typically mild and temporary and may be related to your parasitic infection or the dying parasites. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a comprehensive list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before taking praziquantel, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. This medication may cause dizziness during treatment and up to the day after treatment. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate dizziness. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or engaging in activities requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. This drug passes into breast milk.
